correctness.rationale: A geometric fixed barycentric point has weights constant on every orbit, so fixed support simplices are exactly unions of entire rotation orbits that satisfy all metric edges. Even order orbit contains an n/2-separated antipodal pair, enforcing the final-scale threshold. For odd order, the maximum cyclic distance in two full cosets O_a,O_b is sm+delta_m(a,b), including a=b and m=1. This proves the exact shifted K_m face predicate and respects all inclusions. Independently enumerated 11283 ordered orbit pairs for all n<=55 and every divisor, confirming the odd formula and even individual-orbit diameter. The universal proof uses the coset distance formula, not bounded enumeration.

value.rationale: Complete fixed-point filtration and exact odd/even thresholds are a natural equivariant-topology invariant, address a concrete ingredient of the finite dihedral persistence problem and can be combined with established smaller cyclic ordinary Rips classification, while deliberately not claiming full dihedral Borel equivariant cohomology.

final_claim: For every nontrivial rotational subgroup H_d of finite graph-metric VR K_n(r), odd d=2s+1 has empty fixed space below sm and |K_m(r-sm)| thereafter (m=n/d), with natural inclusion-compatible PL identification; even d has empty fixed space below n/2 and a simplex at n/2.
limitations: Only rotations, not reflections or noncyclic dihedral subgroups; only geometric fixed points of finite abstract complexes, not Borel cohomology.
